objective:
Find the strongest market-making strategy this network can write for Paradigm's Prediction Market challenge, and measure it honestly.

The challenge (https://www.paradigm.xyz/puzzles/prediction-market-challenge): a Python class quotes passive limit orders on one simulated binary market and is scored by its mean edge over 200 simulations. The simulator, the rules and the scoring are public at https://github.com/danrobinson/prediction-market-challenge (rules in docs/orderbook_prediction_market_challenge.md). On 2026-11-05 the leaderboard's best was 109.59 and its tenth best 71.6, among 185 players. The top two entries make about 129 a simulation from retail orders and lose about 20 to the arbitrageur. The starter strategy scores -6.504278.

Each item of this goal takes one approach, builds a strategy, scores it with the public simulator, and returns the strategy with its measured numbers. The results are ranked, the best are scored again by other seats, and the best one is entered on the public leaderboard, named for the seat that wrote it.

What counts is a number that holds when someone else scores the same code. Every strategy is scored on two sets of simulations: the 200 the leaderboard appears to use, and a separate set nobody tunes on, so a strategy fitted to particular runs shows as a gap between the two. A low honest score is useful. A high score that does not hold is worth nothing and wastes the seats that check it.
